走进小小的细胞，比较动物、叶肉植物和细菌的细胞，点一点膜、DNA、细胞核和叶绿体: Explore tiny cells. Compare an animal cell, a leaf mesophyll cell and a bacterium, and inspect their membrane, DNA, nucleus and chloroplasts.
微小世界 · 先认识细胞: THE TINY WORLD · MEET THE CELL
你、树叶和细菌，都与细胞有关。它们很小，却能在里面进行许多生命活动。: You, leaves and bacteria all have something to do with cells. These tiny units carry out many of the activities of life.
身体里的一个小单位: A small unit of a body
叶片里的一个小单位: A small unit of a leaf
细胞结构示意图；使用旁边的结构按钮探索: Cell structure illustration; explore with the structure buttons
先找最外面的一圈膜，再找里面装着大部分 DNA 的细胞核。: First find the outer membrane, then the nucleus holding most of this cell’s DNA.
绿色的小椭圆是叶绿体。注意：这里看的是叶肉细胞，不是所有植物细胞。: The small green ovals are chloroplasts. This is a leaf mesophyll cell; other plant cells can look different.
它也有膜和 DNA，但 DNA 外面没有细胞核的膜。细菌也是细胞！: It has a membrane and DNA, but no nuclear membrane surrounding the DNA. A bacterium is a cell too!
细胞膜把里面与外面分开，也调节一些物质的进出。它不是一堵完全封死的墙。: The cell membrane separates inside from outside and regulates the passage of some substances. It is not a completely sealed wall.
换着看：三种细胞的边界形状一样吗？: Compare them: are the boundaries of all three cells the same shape?
细胞不是空袋子: A cell is not an empty bag
膜里面有细胞质，还有许多参与生命活动的结构。这里仅挑出几个来观察。: Inside the membrane are cytoplasm and many structures that support the cell’s activities. We are exploring just a few of them here.
一个细菌通常就是一个细胞。它有 DNA，却没有膜包围的细胞核。你和树则由许多细胞: A bacterium is usually a single cell. It has DNA, but no membrane-enclosed nucleus. You and a tree are made of many cells.
病毒不是细胞: A virus is not a cell
病毒有遗传物质，但没有完整的细胞结构。它必须借助合适的宿主细胞，才能制造更多病毒: A virus has genetic material but lacks a complete cellular structure. It needs a suitable host cell to make more viruses.
为什么肉眼看不到大多数细胞？: Why can’t we see most cells with our eyes?
因为它们太小了。显微镜帮助我们观察细胞；颜色也常来自染色或后期标记。图中明亮的颜: They are too small. Microscopes help us observe them; colors often come from stains or added labels. The bright colors here help us tell the structures apart.
这是结构比较，不是显微照片或完整细胞模型。形状、颜色、大小和数量都做了教学简化，: This is a structural comparison, not a micrograph or complete cell model. Shapes, colors, sizes and quantities are simplified, and the three illustrations do not share a scale. The animal cell is a typical example with a nucleus; exceptions include mature mammalian red blood cells. The plant example is a leaf mesophyll cell with chloroplasts. Many root cells lack chloroplasts.
DNA 在动物与植物细胞中主要位于细胞核，线粒体也有少量 DNA，植物的叶绿体也: Most DNA in animal and plant cells is in the nucleus. Mitochondria contain a little DNA, and plant chloroplasts have their own DNA too; only the main DNA is highlighted here. The bacterial illustration emphasizes the absence of a membrane-enclosed nucleus; not all bacteria have the same shape. Plants and most bacteria also have a cell wall outside the membrane. The pale central region of the leaf cell represents its vacuole.
这里把细胞称为生命活动的基本单位，不讨论病毒是否算生命的定义争议。页面没有根据外: Here, a cell is described as a basic unit of life’s activities. The page does not address the debate about whether viruses count as living. It does not judge microbes’ harmfulness by appearance or give disease or medication advice.
DNA 携带遗传信息，参与指导细胞制造所需的物质。这个动物细胞的大部分 DNA: DNA carries genetic information that helps guide the cell in making the substances it needs. Most of this animal cell’s DNA is in the nucleus, with a little in its mitochondria.
这个动物细胞有一个膜包围的细胞核，大部分 DNA 保存在里面。细胞核不是会思考的: This animal cell has a membrane-enclosed nucleus holding most of its DNA. The nucleus is not a tiny thinking brain.
动物细胞没有叶绿体。动物不能像绿色叶片那样靠叶绿体进行光合作用。: Animal cells have no chloroplasts. Animals cannot use chloroplasts to photosynthesize the way green leaves do.
植物细胞也有细胞膜！膜外还有一层细胞壁，帮助支撑形状。图上较粗的外圈表示细胞壁。: Plant cells have a cell membrane too! Outside it is a cell wall that helps support the cell’s shape. The thicker outer layer in the illustration is the wall.
叶肉细胞的大部分 DNA 在细胞核里。叶绿体和线粒体也各有少量 DNA，图里没有: Most DNA in a leaf mesophyll cell is in the nucleus. Chloroplasts and mitochondria each contain a little DNA too, which is not drawn separately here.
植物细胞也有膜包围的细胞核。图中的大液泡占了不少地方，把细胞核和其他结构挤到旁边: Plant cells have a membrane-enclosed nucleus too. The large vacuole takes up much of this cell, pushing the nucleus and other structures toward the edge.
叶绿体捕捉光能，参与把水和二氧化碳变成糖的光合作用。很多根部细胞没有叶绿体，所以: Chloroplasts capture light energy for photosynthesis, which makes sugars from water and carbon dioxide. Many root cells have no chloroplasts, so not every plant cell looks like this.
细菌虽小，也有把内部和外部隔开的细胞膜。大多数细菌在膜外还有细胞壁，但它与植物的: Small as it is, a bacterium has a cell membrane separating inside from outside. Most bacteria also have a cell wall, though it differs from a plant cell wall.
细菌也有 DNA！它主要集中在细胞内的一个区域，叫拟核；这里没有一层核膜把 DN: Bacteria have DNA too! It is mainly concentrated in a region called the nucleoid. No nuclear membrane surrounds this DNA.
细菌没有膜包围的细胞核，但这不等于没有 DNA。点一下 DNA，看遗传物质在什么: Bacteria have no membrane-enclosed nucleus, but that does not mean they have no DNA. Tap DNA to see where their genetic material is.
细菌没有叶绿体。不过，有些细菌能用自己的光合结构进行光合作用，例如蓝细菌。: Bacteria have no chloroplasts. Some bacteria, such as cyanobacteria, can still photosynthesize using their own photosynthetic structures.
试着找：哪个细胞的 DNA 没有被细胞核包住？: Can you find the cell whose DNA is not enclosed in a nucleus?
有没有细胞核，能帮助我们分辨这几类细胞。: The presence or absence of a nucleus helps us distinguish these types of cells.
记住这个例外：植物的根部细胞通常没有叶绿体。: Remember this exception: plant root cells usually have no chloroplasts.

线粒体有外膜和向内折叠的内膜，参与把营养物质中的能量转成细胞可用的形式。能量不是: A mitochondrion has an outer membrane and a folded inner membrane. It helps convert energy in nutrients into forms the cell can use. Energy is not created from nothing.
这个动物细胞没有像叶肉细胞那样占据中央的大液泡。动物细胞仍可有较小的囊泡。: This animal cell has no large central vacuole like the leaf cell. Animal cells can still contain smaller vesicles.
植物细胞也有线粒体，也从糖等物质中释放可用能量。植物的呼吸作用白天和夜晚都能进行: Plant cells also have mitochondria and release usable energy from sugars and other substances. Plants can respire during both day and night.
中央浅色的大液泡含有细胞液，有自己的膜。它帮助储存物质、调节水分，并与细胞壁一起: The pale central vacuole contains cell sap and has its own membrane. It helps store substances and regulate water, contributing with the cell wall to cell support.
细菌没有线粒体，却也能进行能量转换。不同细菌使用的物质和方式不同，不能把这两段动: Bacteria have no mitochondria but still convert energy. Their materials and processes vary, so these animal and plant examples cannot represent all bacteria.
这张典型细菌图没有植物中央大液泡。微生物的内部结构有许多差异，这里只比较选出的结: This representative bacterium has no plant-like central vacuole. Microbial interiors vary; only selected structures are compared here.
把植物细胞也选来看看：它不只制造糖，也会利用糖。: Look at the plant cell too: it both makes and uses sugars.
放大浅色中央区域，再找它外侧的薄薄细胞质。: Enlarge the pale central region, then find the thin surrounding cytoplasm.
半透明表面盖在原有结构上；切回剖视可看清内部。: The translucent surface covers the same structures. Return to the cutaway for a clear interior view.
虚线框与放大窗口对应同一处；膜和细胞器都经过教学放大。: The dashed frame and close-up show the same location. Membranes and organelles are enlarged for teaching.
有光时，叶肉细胞制造糖: With light, a leaf cell makes sugars
细菌也有多样的生命活动: Bacteria have varied life processes too
光提供能量。水和二氧化碳参与变化，形成糖，并释放氧气。糖留在细胞里，也可以供植物: Light supplies energy. Water and carbon dioxide contribute to making sugars and releasing oxygen. Sugars can remain in the cell or supply other parts of the plant.
这里看有氧呼吸的例子：糖等营养物质与氧参与一连串变化，细胞获得可用能量，并产生二: This is an aerobic respiration example. Nutrients such as sugars and oxygen take part in a series of changes, supplying usable energy and forming carbon dioxide and water.
细菌也会交换物质、利用能量。它们的方式很多，这里保留结构比较，不用同一段动画代表: Bacteria also exchange materials and use energy in many ways. Here we compare their structure without making one animation stand for all bacteria.
进入：二氧化碳、水；光带来能量: Inputs: carbon dioxide and water; light supplies energy
进入：糖等营养物质、氧: Inputs: nutrients such as sugars, and oxygen
形成：二氧化碳、水；获得可用能量: Carbon dioxide and water form; usable energy is made available
金色六边形表示糖，蓝色小滴表示水；小点不按真实分子数量。: Gold hexagons represent sugars and blue drops represent water. Marker counts are not molecular quantities.
细胞内的金色光环表示能量可被利用，不是另一种流出去的物质。部分能量转为热。: The gold ring inside the cell means energy can be used. It is not another substance flowing out. Some energy becomes heat.

箭头概括多步变化，不是细胞内固定的管道；小点数量不代表化学反应的比例。营养物质的: Paths summarize many steps, not fixed pipes inside a cell. Marker counts are not reaction ratios. Nutrient breakdown begins in the cytoplasm, with mitochondria involved in later steps.
这是结构与两种行为的示意，不是显微照片或完整细胞模型。形状、颜色、大小和数量都做: These structures and two processes are teaching diagrams, not micrographs or complete cell models. Shape, colour, size and counts are simplified, and the three drawings do not share a scale. The animal example has a nucleus; specialised cells such as mature mammalian red blood cells differ. The plant example is a chloroplast-containing mesophyll cell, unlike many root cells.
行为画面只比较典型动物细胞的有氧呼吸与叶肉细胞的光合作用、呼吸作用。呼吸不是把空: The process views compare aerobic respiration in a typical animal cell with photosynthesis and respiration in a leaf cell. Cellular respiration involves chemical reactions, not tiny lungs. Photosynthetic oxygen comes from water; sugar carbon comes from carbon dioxide. Sugars can be used, stored or supplied elsewhere. These processes can overlap in reality. Animation order and speed aid observation without modelling concentrations, temperature, light intensity, ATP yield or net gas exchange.

糖和氧来到细胞里，沿着路径继续观察。: Follow sugars and oxygen on their way through the cell.
糖先在细胞质中分解；金色小块会继续移动。: Sugar first breaks down in the cytoplasm. The gold pieces keep moving.
跟着金色小块：它们与氧来到同一处线粒体区域，参与后续多步变化。: Follow the gold pieces and oxygen to the same mitochondrial region, where further reactions take place.
这里正在转换能量：形成 ATP，也形成二氧化碳和水。: Energy is being converted here: ATP forms, as do carbon dioxide and water.
跟着金色 ATP：它把可用能量带给细胞活动。: Follow the gold ATP: it carries usable energy to cell activities.
看，小块连接起来了！ATP 支持细胞制造所需物质。: Look, the pieces join together! ATP helps the cell build materials it needs.
用起来：支持细胞制造物质。: Put to use: helping the cell build materials.
送到需要处：ATP 在细胞内传递可用能量。: To where it is needed: ATP transfers usable energy within the cell.
正在形成 ATP：糖中的一部分能量转成可用形式。: ATP is forming: some energy from sugar is captured in a usable form.
留意线粒体旁将出现的金色 ATP，再跟着它看能量用在哪里。: Watch for gold ATP beside the mitochondrion. Then follow it to see where the energy is used.
金色 ATP 标记表示携带可用能量的分子；绿色小块表示制造物质的原料。棕色波纹表: Gold ATP marks molecules carrying usable energy; green pieces are building materials. Brown waves show some energy becoming heat. The cell is not really glowing.
糖先在细胞质中分解，分解后的物质继续进入线粒体；氧参与后续反应。圈出的区域把多步: Sugar breakdown begins in the cytoplasm; its products continue into mitochondria, where oxygen takes part in later reactions. The ring groups several steps together: sugar and oxygen do not simply collide and turn into energy. Paths are not fixed pipes, and symbols do not show molecular ratios.
行为画面只比较典型动物细胞的有氧呼吸与叶肉细胞的光合作用、呼吸作用。呼吸不是把空: The process view compares aerobic respiration in a typical animal cell with photosynthesis and respiration in a leaf cell. Cellular respiration is a set of nutrient-using reactions, not tiny lungs inhaling air. Oxygen released by photosynthesis comes mainly from water; sugar carbon comes from carbon dioxide. Sugars can be used, stored or transported. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm, does not directly use oxygen and also produces ATP. Pyruvate then enters mitochondria, where oxygen is used at the end of the respiratory chain. The animation groups later oxidation, ATP production and products in one observation region; it omits enzymes, electron transfer and the proton gradient across the inner membrane. ATP carries usable chemical energy. After helping power processes such as synthesis, it becomes ADP and other products and can be recycled; it is not free-floating energy. Real processes can overlap. Sequence and speed aid observation and do not model concentrations, temperature, light intensity, ATP quantities or net gas exchange.

Cellular respiration is a set of nutrient-using reactions, not tiny lungs inhaling air. Oxygen released by photosynthesis comes mainly from water; sugar carbon comes from carbon dioxide. Sugars can be used, stored or transported. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm, does not directly use oxygen and also produces ATP. Pyruvate then enters mitochondria, where oxygen is used at the end of the respiratory chain. The animation groups later oxidation, ATP production and products in one observation region; it omits enzymes, electron transfer and the proton gradient across the inner membrane.
